key_insight: Group Reservoir Computing uses a reservoir-computing model grounded in Wei–Norman decomposition to synthesize quantum gates with unitary dynamics by construction.
engineering_relevance: It offers a low-training-cost route to generate control pulses for finite-dimensional quantum hardware and can accelerate standard gradient-based gate optimization.
method: Encode gate dynamics with Wei–Norman coordinates for a compact evolution model.
Train a reservoir with a single linear regression to predict control pulses.
Use the learned pulse as a direct synthesis output or as a warm-start for gradient refinement.
evidence_signal: On the standard single-qubit gate set, the method achieved mean fidelity 0.94 over eight benchmark gates and roughly halved the iterations needed by plain gradient ascent to hit a target fidelity.
watch_item: The reported gains are strongest for single-qubit benchmarks, so scaling behavior and hardware-specific control constraints will need careful validation for larger multiqubit systems.
paper_title: A Reservoir Computing Approach to Quantum Gate Synthesis
